# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind. I can hear speech and physically cut wires on the bomb, but I cannot see anything (neither colours, bomb markings, nor gestures). 

Deaf can see the bomb and speak, but cannot hear.
Mute can hear and read the manual, but cannot speak.

Since Deaf cannot hear me, my speech will only reach Mute. Deaf's turn is next; Deaf should speak aloud to describe the bomb, which Mute and I will both hear. Mute can then look up the solution in the manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (using ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Deaf will see the gesture and speak the instruction aloud so I can hear it and cut the correct wire.

I will send this coordination message to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf can see the bomb and speak, but cannot hear. You can hear and gesture, but cannot speak. I can hear and cut wires (positions 1-3), but cannot see. Deaf speaks after me. Once Deaf describes the bomb, check your manual. Then gesture to Deaf (☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Deaf will see your gesture and speak aloud to tell me which wire to cut.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture the instruction to me (e.g. ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3). Blind, wait for Mute's instructions via me.

Deaf described the bomb at the end of Round 1: Display 0, Light blue, Wires: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green.
In Round 2, Mute went first and has presumably consulted the manual and gestured the solution to Deaf.
I cannot see gestures, and Deaf speaks after me in this round. Deaf will translate Mute's gesture into speech at the end of Round 2, which I will receive at the start of Round 3.

Therefore, I must wait for Deaf's callout before cutting any wire.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The light has changed from blue to RED. Display is still 0. Wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute just gestured a flat hand ? to me. Blind, did you touch anything? Blind and Mute: does ? mean WAIT/HOLD, or does it refer to something else? Mute, if you mean WAIT, gesture ?. If you mean cut a wire, gesture ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3. If you mean hold the button, gesture ?.

I have not touched the bomb. Since Deaf goes after me, Deaf will see what Mute gestured in Turn 3 and speak the instruction to me at the end of this round.

I will speak to Mute to confirm I haven't touched anything and remind them to keep gestures unambiguous, then wait for Deaf's callout.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have not touched anything. I cannot see gestures. Mute, please gesture clearly to Deaf which wire to cut: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Light is now WHITE. Display is 0. Mute confirmed ? (WAIT). Blind: the light seems to be cycling colors every round (Turn 1 blue, Turn 2 red, Turn 3 white). Do NOT touch anything yet. Mute: please tell me what the ultimate action is and when to do it. You can send multiple gestures in one turn! For example: gesture the wire number (?/?/?) or button action (? for press/hold), followed by the trigger color: 🔵 or gesture for the color/time. Or Mute, just keep gesturing ? while we must wait, and when the current round is the EXACT moment to act, gesture the action symbol (? wire 1, ? wire 2, ? wire 3, or ? press). Blind, be ready to act the instant I call it.

Deaf confirmed that Mute is having us wait for a specific condition/light color. Blind goes before Deaf, so Deaf will relay Mute's instruction at the end of Turn 4. I will wait for Deaf's command.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Light is now GREEN. Display is still 0. Attention Mute and Blind: Blind cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear speech. That means Blind speaks to Mute, Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to Blind! Blind, if you are asking questions or describing what you feel, Mute must relay it to me using gestures, and I will speak for you. Mute: you gestured ? three times. Does ? mean WAIT? If ? means WAIT, gesture ? next. If you need Blind to do something, please define a system: ?=Wire 1, ?=Wire 2, ?=Wire 3. Or gesture ? if you want me to list options. Mute, tell me what to say to Blind!

I will instruct Mute on how to clarify the signal to Deaf, while waiting for Deaf's explicit instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf cannot hear, but Deaf can read your gestures. Deaf is confused about whether your gesture meant WAIT or WIRE 3. If you want me to cut a wire, use ☝ for Wire 1, ✌ for Wire 2, or 🤟 for Wire 3, so Deaf clearly announces 'CUT WIRE X'. If we need to wait, use ✋. Please make it obvious to Deaf so Deaf says the exact wire number to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Understood, Mute: ? ? means 'Yes, keep waiting.' But remember: the light changes every round! If Blind must act on a specific color, Blind must know the rule in advance so they can act in time. Mute, please tell me the target color and the action using gestures: For colors, use: 🔵 (or gesture 1=blue ?, 2=red ?, 3=white ?, 4=green ?, 5=yellow ?). For action: ?=Cut Wire 1, ?=Cut Wire 2, ?=Cut Wire 3, ?=Press button. If Blind spoke and told you something, gesture 🗣. Blind: what do you feel under your hands? Describe it out loud so Mute hears you.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: My only possible action is cutting a wire: positions 1, 2, or 3. There are NO buttons to press or hold, only three wires. Please tell Deaf which wire to cut and on which light color, or signal Deaf when it's time so Deaf can tell me.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no new instructions from Deaf yet. Mute moved at the start of this turn (Turn 7), gesturing to Deaf. Deaf will take their turn next and speak the instruction aloud to me, which I will receive at the start of Turn 8. 

I will speak to Mute to ensure they conveyed the exact action and light color to Deaf, and I will wait for Deaf's callout.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, please ensure you clearly gestured to Deaf which wire (1, 2, or 3) and on which light color to cut. Deaf speaks next and will tell me.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind and Mute, listen carefully! Mute decoded the manual using our code: When light is Blue, cut Wire 2. When light is White, cut Wire 1. When light is Yellow, cut Wire 3. The light cycles: Turn 8 (next round) will be WHITE! Turn 9 Green, Turn 10 Yellow, Turn 11 Blue. Blind: in Turn 8 the light will be WHITE. Mute, gesture ? if Blind should cut Wire 1 on Turn 8 (White light), or gesture ? if we need a different one. Blind, if Mute gestures ?, cut Wire 1!

I received Deaf's message at the start of Turn 8: Deaf explained that according to Mute's manual instructions, when the light is White, cut Wire 1. Deaf also confirmed that Turn 8 is White.

Since I cannot see gestures and Deaf speaks after me, waiting until Turn 9 would mean the light is no longer White (Deaf noted Turn 9 will be Green). Therefore, cutting Wire 1 during Turn 8 while the light is White is the required action.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
